scenario: You had a valid reason for missing the deadline to file your income tax return, and that delay has since been approved. You now need to submit the return and want to know how to do it.

You are being sent to work in another country that has a social-security agreement with India. You want proof that your Indian coverage continues so you do not end up paying social-security contributions twice.
You joined an establishment where provident-fund rules do not currently apply. You want to know whether you can still become a PF member.
Your basic pay has gone above the usual PF wage limit after you joined the scheme. You want to know whether you can remain a member and how your contributions are handled.
You work through a contractor and your PF contributions do not seem to be reaching your account. You want to know who is responsible and how the payments can be checked.
Your former employer has closed down, and no one is available to sign your PF withdrawal papers. You need to know how you can still submit the claim.
You have just started a job and want to understand how PF savings, employer contributions, transfers between jobs, withdrawals, and nominations work.
Your employer has not deposited PF dues for some months, and you are worried about what that means for the money due to you. You want to know how the unpaid amount is handled.
You are covered by PF and want to know whether any part of your salary is deducted separately for the life-insurance benefit linked to your employment.
You left a job and noticed that your PF and pension records may show different exit dates. You want to know when that can happen and what the dates should look like.
You married your spouse after retirement and want to know whether she would still qualify for family pension if you die first.
You make large cash withdrawals from your bank account and want to know whether tax is deducted once your withdrawals cross certain yearly amounts.
You have a problem with your income-tax account but are not registered on the tax portal. You want to raise a complaint and later check what happened to it.
You are filing a return for income from a small business and have chosen the simplified business return. You previously chose one tax regime and now need to make the correct choice for this year.
You are working but have not received any wages yet. You want to know whether PF membership can start before you are actually paid.
You received a tax-department appreciation certificate a few years ago, but your PAN now has a linking problem. You want to know whether you can still view the old certificate.
You help taxpayers with their filings as a tax filing agent and need to know which services you are actually allowed to perform for a client online.
You are handling the PF account of a family member who died without naming a nominee. You want to know who can receive the PF money.

You have built up about eight years of pensionable service and are considering taking the money available to you now. You want to understand what you would give up compared with waiting until you can receive a pension.
Your old PF account is marked inactive, but you are working again. You want to know whether you should move that balance to your current account or withdraw it.
Your employer has defaulted on PF payments, and you want to know what action can be taken to recover the unpaid dues.
You work for an organization connecting its tax systems to the department and have finished the required testing. You need to know what happens before you can start using the live service.
You are nearing retirement and want to know when your monthly pension can start, including what happens if you leave work before age 58.
You work with a government-recognized research facility and need to check whether a client’s research-related tax filing has been completed and whether anything is still pending.
You are a chartered accountant and need to create your professional account on the income-tax portal so you can handle tax work there.
You want to know who in your workplace is covered by the work-linked life insurance and what financial benefit the family may receive if you die while employed.
You filed an income-tax return but did not verify it within the required time. You want to know what happens now and how you can complete the verification.
You were told after a tax search that you must file a return covering income that was uncovered. You need to know what the submission involves and how to complete it.
You have a demat account and want to use it to verify tax-related submissions. The account is not going through validation, so you need to know what information must match and how to fix it.

Your payslip shows that PF was deducted from your wages, but the money is not appearing in your PF account. You want to know what can be done when an employer keeps the deduction but does not deposit it.
You are responsible for tax work for a research facility and want one place to see its filing activity, pending work, and other tax-related tasks.
You are helping the parents of an EPF member who died without an eligible spouse or child. They want to know whether they can receive the pension as dependents.
You regularly withdraw large amounts of cash and want to know when the bank or post office has to deduct tax from those withdrawals and whether any exemptions apply to you.
You are over 75, live in India, and receive only a pension and bank interest. You want to know whether you still need to send an annual tax return.
You are planning for retirement and want to understand how the employee pension scheme works, how long membership lasts, and what benefits may be available to your family.
You earn around the PF wage ceiling and want to know whether you meet the basic service requirements for pension benefits.
You left your job but want to keep adding money to your PF account yourself. You need to know whether contributions can continue without an employer.
You are caring for a child whose both parents had pension contributions and have died. You want to know whether the child can receive pension linked to both parents.
You generated a tax-payment reference but cannot pay today. You want to know how long it remains usable before it expires.

Your salary or savings account already had tax taken out, and you are preparing your return. You want to know whether that income still has to be reported and how to receive credit for the tax withheld.
You have reached 58 but do not need the pension immediately. You want to know whether you can start it later and how waiting would affect the amount.
You have built up pensionable service and are comparing retirement options. You want to understand what kinds of pension payments and family benefits the pension scheme can provide.
You filed your return and the tax you paid does not match the tax showing in your tax records. You need to find the mismatch and understand what to correct.
You have salary, a house, and other income and are trying to decide which income-tax return fits your situation. You want to know which common exclusions might rule a particular return out.
You resigned from your job and want to withdraw your PF immediately. You need to know whether there is a waiting period after leaving.
You want to know what financial support your family might receive from the work-linked life cover if you die while still employed, and how quickly a claim is normally settled.
Your organization is setting up access to a tax reporting service and has been asked for proof of the person responsible for the technical connection. You want to know what documentation is needed.
You can see interest being added to your PF balance and want to understand how that interest is calculated and credited over time.
You changed jobs and have pensionable service from your previous employer. You want to know what record helps preserve that service for future pension and family benefits.
You have more than one demat account and want to use one for electronic tax verification. You need to know whether you can enable verification on more than one account.
You earn above the usual PF wage limit and still want PF coverage. You want to know whether you can opt in and how the contributions would work.
Your internet connection is unreliable and you prefer preparing your income-tax return offline. You want to know which offline tool to use and how the finished return is submitted.
You are a retired pensioner living far from the office that handles your pension. You want to submit proof that you are alive without making a physical visit.
You want a rough idea of how your years of service and pensionable pay could affect the monthly pension you receive after retirement.
You receive a pension and need to provide your regular life certificate. You want to know when it is due and whether you can submit it digitally instead of visiting a bank or office.
You can no longer remember the password for your income-tax account and need to regain access using one of the available verification methods.
You filed a return but forgot to verify it and now want to start over. You need to know whether the earlier unverified submission can be cancelled before filing again.
You are new to provident-fund savings and want to understand what the scheme is, who administers it, and what kind of retirement protection it provides.
Your employer deposited PF contributions late, and you are worried that you lost interest for those months. You want to know whether the delay changes the interest due to you.

scenario: You paid a tax bill online but the payment is not showing yet. You want to know how to check whether it went through and what to do when the bank has not reported it.
You want a quick ballpark of your tax under two available choices before filing. You need to know whether that number can be relied on as the final amount.
You retired around the period when the pension rules changed and are confused about which part of your past salary is used to calculate your pension.
You want one place to see your recent tax returns, forms, tax deposits, refunds, grievances, and anything that still needs your action.
Your employer refuses or is unavailable to sign your PF withdrawal claim. You need to know what other route is available for submitting the application.
Your PF balance moved to your new job, but you do not see a separate pension balance transfer. You want to know whether something went wrong with your pension record.

scenario: Your mobile number or email address has changed and you need to update the contact details on your income-tax account. You want to know what verification will be needed.
You heard that part of a pension could once be exchanged for a lump sum. You want to know what this means and whether that option is still available.
You would rather have a tax filing agent handle your return and some follow-up work for you. You want to know what they can do and how many such agents can be active at once.
You paid for insurance, retirement savings, or other expenses during the year that may qualify for tax relief. You want to know which payments can be claimed and what limits apply.
You need to pay income tax online and are choosing between bank-based and other payment methods. You want to know how the payment works and what you can keep as proof afterward.
You are still working after age 58 and want to know whether you can start receiving your pension without leaving the job.
You have hired a chartered accountant and want to give them access to handle a particular tax form, extend their authorization, or stop their access later.
You are preparing your income-tax return and want to check the common questions that taxpayers often run into before you submit it.
You use the tax department’s mobile app and want a quick four-digit sign-in option so you do not have to enter the full password each time.

You work for an organization that has to report certain financial transactions to the tax department. You need to set up the organization’s reporting identity and authorize someone to submit the reports.
You left your job and are considering leaving your PF balance untouched for a while. You want to know how long it can remain there and whether it keeps earning interest.
You are trying to understand why a surviving spouse may receive a different pension amount depending on whether the member had already started receiving a pension.
You are an individual with more than one house and some investment income, and you also sold an asset during the year. You want to know how these different sources of income fit into your return.

You manage tax matters for a trust and want another person to help with filings without giving them unrestricted control over the account. You need to understand what that person can do and what happens if their authority is revoked.
You are filing the simplified return for a small business and want to claim tax that was already deducted from your income. The return is asking you to identify why that tax was deducted.
Your employer has fewer than 20 employees, but you and most of your coworkers want PF coverage. You want to know whether joining is possible.
You want pension coverage without putting money into PF and are wondering whether the pension part can be separated from PF membership.
You are having trouble deciding how to sign in to your income-tax account and want to know which login methods are available besides the usual password.
You received an online tax notice proposing a correction and you disagree with one of the proposed changes. You want to know how to view the notice and send your response.
Your employer missed pension contributions for part of your service, and you want to know whether you can still receive a withdrawal benefit for that period.
You are on the tax website and a support agent offers to guide you remotely. You want to let them see the page you are viewing without giving them your password.

You have completed a tax audit report and already obtained its professional identification number, but the portal will not let you enter that number during filing. You want to know whether you can still submit the report and update the identifier later.
You saw PF deducted from your wages but the amount was not deposited by your employer. You want to know what action can be taken to recover the missing contribution.
You already receive a pension under the scheme and are taking another job. You want to know whether you need to join PF again and whether you can join the pension part again.
You are unmarried and want to nominate someone who is not a family member. You want to know what happens to that nomination if your family situation changes later.
You are the family of an ex-serviceman who dies while covered by the pension scheme. You want to know whether an additional survivor benefit may be available alongside the military pension.

You bought a home with a loan and also paid for things such as insurance or provident-fund contributions. You want to know what details you need to report if you plan to claim deductions under the old tax regime.

You have a creditor trying to recover money from you, and you are worried that your PF savings could be seized to cover the debt. You want to know whether PF money has any protection from such action.
You want to understand how employer payments support the work-linked life cover and what parts of your employment record can affect the amount your family may receive after your death.
You need a copy of a tax form you filed earlier and want to know whether it can be downloaded and whether anything in a filed form can still be edited.
You are responsible for people working in an establishment covered by the pension scheme and need to understand who must enroll workers, maintain records, and make the required contributions.
You live outside India and have income from sources such as salary or investments. You are unsure which income-tax return is appropriate for your situation.
You are registering your organization with the tax department so it can use reporting and verification services. You want to know what contact details and authorization proof are needed.
You are a pensioner who has moved away from the city where your pension was set up. You want to keep receiving payments without travelling back just to submit your life certificate.

You started filling your income-tax return online but now want to switch to the offline tool without entering everything again. You need to know whether the partly completed return can be carried over.

You want a quick tax estimate using information already available about your income and tax deducted, and you want to compare two tax-regime choices before filing. You also want to know whether the estimate should be treated as final.
You want to put more than the usual employee PF contribution into your account. You need to know how much extra you can contribute and whether your employer has to match it.
You have just started earning and want to understand whether PF applies to you, what you and your employer put in, and how you can access the money later.

You are dealing with the estate of a deceased member who had two legally recognized marriages, and both spouses are seeking family pension. You want to understand how the pension is handled between the surviving spouses.
You are helping a family after a member died leaving children from two marriages. You want to know how children from the different marriages are treated when deciding eligibility for child pension.
You are not sure which income-tax return fits your income and want the portal to guide you through a few questions before choosing a form.
You have a court-related debt and worry that your PF savings might be attached to cover it. You want to know whether retirement savings have any protection.
You worked in India under a social-security agreement and have since returned to your home country. You want to know whether your pension can be paid there.
Your date of birth in your PF records is wrong, and you have documents showing the correct date. You want to know whether the record can be corrected and what proof is needed.
You are planning for pension and want to know which part of your past wages is used to work out the pensionable salary.
You are already logged in to your income-tax account and want to replace your current password with a new one.
You have tried to resolve a PF problem and now need to file a formal complaint and keep track of whether it has been resolved.
You qualify for pension based on higher wages and are confused about which salary history will be used to calculate your pension.
You worked in India under a social-security agreement but still have less than the usual pensionable service. You want to know whether a withdrawal benefit is available when you leave.
You are checking your payslip and want to know whether money for the pension and work-linked life-insurance parts of PF is also deducted from your salary.
Your PAN and Aadhaar carry different personal details, so linking is failing. You want to know what to correct and what to try if the records still refuse to connect.
You filed an updated return and received a notice saying something in it is defective. You need to send a corrected response and are unsure which filing basis to use.
You created a tax-payment reference earlier and chose card payment but did not finish the transaction. You now want to return and complete that payment.
You have hired a chartered accountant and want to add them to your tax account and assign a particular filing task to them. You also want to know how to stop or reactivate their access later.

Your organization is enrolling as an external tax-reporting agency and has been asked to prove its identity and who is responsible for the account. You want to know which documents are needed before you submit the request.
You retired and left your PF money in the account. You want to know how long it will continue earning interest after you stop working.
You are self-employed and want to join PF on your own without working for a covered employer. You want to know whether that is possible.

You earn income from a small business or profession and have interest from loans for things such as education, a home, or an electric vehicle. You want to know what return details are needed to claim the relevant deductions.
You created a tax-payment reference but have not paid yet. You want to know when it will expire and where you can still see it afterward.
You have a valid PAN but have never created an online tax account. You want to know what contact information is needed and whether each family member needs a separate account.
You have a new family member and want your PF records to reflect the change. You need to know how to submit the update and whether it can be done electronically.
You used a tax intermediary and received verification messages for a request they submitted on your behalf. You want to confirm the request before the service is completed.
You need to pay income tax and are choosing among several payment methods. You want to know whether you can change the payment method after the payment reference has already been created.
You filed a return and noticed that the tax deducted, collected, or paid by you does not match the tax records. You want to locate the mismatch and see the details clearly.
You have a tax matter to sort out and need to know which assessing officer is responsible for your PAN.

You have a processed tax return that appears to contain a mistake, leaving you with a smaller refund or a larger amount to pay. You want to know whether you can ask for a correction and where to see its status.
You expect to retire several years from now and want to know which pension rules will determine your pension when you eventually start receiving it.
You tried linking PAN and Aadhaar but were told a fee has to be paid first. You want to know how to make the payment and then finish the linking process.
You are an international worker from a country without a social-security agreement with India and are leaving India. You want to know whether a pension-related withdrawal benefit is available.
You run an organization that deducts or collects tax for other people and need to know whether you need a separate identifier for those tax-related filings.

You are an authorized tax intermediary managing a client’s account and need to check a mismatch, correction request, refund reissue, or grievance on the client’s behalf. You want to know which of these actions you can perform.
You are helping a family after a member died leaving children, including a married daughter. You want to know whether marriage affects a child's eligibility for pension.
You keep getting an access-denied message when trying to enter the income-tax portal through net banking. You want to know what needs to be enabled before that login method will work.
You have a straightforward salary-based tax situation and want to submit your annual return online. You may have a saved draft already and need to know how to continue from there.
You have a processed tax return with a correction request that was rejected, or an intimation with a mistake that still needs fixing. You want to know what correction options remain.
Your employer says the percentage going into PF may be lower for a while. You are concerned about whether that changes the pension you will eventually receive.

You already have an idea which tax return you should file, but you want to check that the form and supporting schedules fit your income. You also want to be able to change your answers if you realize you chose the wrong option.
You paid interest on a loan for education, a home, or an electric vehicle and want to know what loan details you need to keep ready when claiming the deduction.
You want to confirm a filed tax return electronically through a verified financial account. You need to know what setup is required and whether paper confirmation is still needed afterward.
You signed in to the tax portal and see a pending compliance item, but you are not sure whether it needs a response or is simply something you should review.
You received a tax notice by email and want to make sure it really came from the tax department before you act on it.
You applied to become an authorized tax intermediary and your registration is pending or has a document problem. You need to know how to check the status and what to do about the defect.
You suspect your employer deducted PF from your wages but did not deposit the same amount. You want a record that shows what contributions were actually recovered.
You started receiving pension long ago and had part of the pension exchanged for a lump sum. You want to know when the original monthly pension amount can be restored.
You are a pensioner who took a partial pension lump sum many years ago and want to know whether you are covered by the rules for restoring the full monthly pension.
